title: Licenses, permits, zoning and home businesses

sources.claim: The SBA lists the launch steps (choose a structure, register, get federal and state tax IDs, apply for licenses and permits, open a business bank account, get insurance) as a general guide.

sections.skill: Identify which permissions to check for an activity and place

questions.prompt: Lucy wants to sell homemade baked goods from her kitchen. What should she check?

choices.text: Local and state rules for selling food made at home
Only whether her friends and neighbors like her cookies
Only how to post on social media
Only the price of flour at the store

questions.correct_answer: Local and state rules for selling food made at home
questions.intro: Many activities need permission from a government before you start. A BUSINESS LICENSE is general permission to operate in a city or county. A PERMIT covers a specific activity, such as selling food, putting up a sign, or doing construction. ZONING rules say what activities are allowed at a location, including homes; some neighborhoods limit customer visits, signs, parking or noise. Some jobs, such as hair care or electrical work, need a professional license. Rules depend on the activity and the place: city, county, state and sometimes federal. Rental leases and homeowner associations can add limits.
questions.feedback: Food sales often have specific rules.

questions.intro: Think of permission slips at school: one lets you go on a field trip, another lets you play a sport. A business may need several kinds: a general business license (permission to operate), a permit for a specific activity (like serving food), and approval that the location allows the activity (zoning). Some people also need a personal professional license, like a driver's license for a job. Each comes from the group in charge of that rule.
questions.feedback: It is broad permission.
